title: Hereditary discrepancy and factorization norms (AimPL) — Problem 1.1: Constructive Komlós

problems.sourceStatement: Find a polynomial time algorithm to find the signs above.
problems.problem: Design a polynomial-time algorithm that, given vectors $v_1, \dots, v_n$ in the Euclidean unit ball of $\mathbb{R}^d$, finds signs $\epsilon_i \in \{-1, 1\}$ achieving the strongest known (Komlós-type) discrepancy guarantee on $\|\sum_i \epsilon_i v_i\|_\infty$.
problems.wordDescription: Banaszczyk's bound $O(\sqrt{\log \min\{d, n\}})$ for the Komlós problem was originally non-constructive, and the question of finding the signs efficiently was a major challenge. The workshop-era status was a constructive $O(\log \min\{d, n\})$ bound via the partial-coloring based algorithms of Bansal and of Lovett-Meka and the convex-geometric algorithm of Rothvoss. Shortly after the workshop this gap was closed: Bansal, Dadush and Garg (FOCS 2016) gave a polynomial-time algorithm matching Banaszczyk's bound for the Komlós problem, and Bansal, Dadush, Garg and Lovett then gave a constructive version of the full Banaszczyk vector-balancing theorem (the Gram-Schmidt walk), with an alternative multiplicative-weight-update approach by Dadush, Garg, Lovett and Nikolov. The problem as posed is therefore essentially resolved: the remaining gap between the achievable constructive bound and a constant is exactly the Komlós conjecture itself.
problems.mathematicalConditions: Design a randomized (or deterministic) polynomial-time algorithm that, on input $v_1, \dots, v_n \in \mathbb{R}^d$ with $\|v_i\|_2 \leq 1$, outputs a coloring $\epsilon \in \{-1, 1\}^n$ with $\left\|\sum_{i=1}^n \epsilon_i v_i\right\|_\infty \leq f(d, n)$, where $f(d, n) = O(\sqrt{\log \min\{d, n\}})$ matches Banaszczyk's non-constructive bound.

literature.title: N. Bansal, Constructive algorithms for discrepancy minimization, FOCS 2010
literature.description: The breakthrough SDP-based algorithm that first made classical discrepancy bounds (including Spencer's theorem and $O(\sqrt{t} \log n)$ for the $t$-sparse setting) constructive.

literature.title: S. Lovett, R. Meka, Constructive discrepancy minimization by walking on the edges, FOCS 2012; SIAM Journal on Computing 44(5):1573-1605, 2015
literature.description: A simpler random-walk ('edge-walk') algorithm matching Spencer's theorem; the partial-coloring machinery adapted to it yields the constructive $O(\log \min\{d, n\})$ bound for the Komlós problem.

literature.title: T. Rothvoss, Constructive discrepancy minimization for convex sets, FOCS 2014
literature.description: A convex-geometric approach via Gaussian measure and separation oracles that also yields constructive bounds for the Komlós problem.

literature.title: N. Bansal, D. Dadush, S. Garg, An algorithm for Komlós conjecture matching Banaszczyk's bound, FOCS 2016
literature.description: First polynomial-time algorithm achieving Banaszczyk's $O(\sqrt{\log \min\{d, n\}})$ bound for the Komlós problem, resolving the constructive-Komlós question up to the conjecture itself.

literature.title: D. Dadush, S. Garg, S. Lovett, A. Nikolov, Towards a constructive version of Banaszczyk's vector balancing theorem, SoCG 2016; Theory of Computing 15(15):1-58, 2019
literature.description: Multiplicative-weight-update based algorithm for the general vector-balancing theorem of Banaszczyk; also discusses the tightness of the Gaussian measure threshold $1/2$.

literature.title: N. Bansal, D. Dadush, S. Garg, S. Lovett, The Gram-Schmidt walk: a cure for the Banaszczyk blues, STOC 2018
literature.description: Constructive algorithm matching Banaszczyk's theorem for arbitrary convex bodies (beyond cubes), subsuming the constructive Komlós and Beck-Fiala results.

problems.verificationNotes: Verified on 2026-08-25. The page's status '$O(\log min\{d,n\})$ [Bansal'10, Lovett-Meka'14, Rothvoss'15]' matches the workshop-era state of the art: Garg's thesis (TU Eindhoven, 2018) states that 'partial coloring, and the algorithms for it, can be adapted to give an O(log n) bound for the Komlós setting'. The later improvement to $O(\sqrt{\log \min\{d, n\}})$ by Bansal-Dadush-Garg (FOCS 2016) and Bansal-Dadush-Garg-Lovett (Gram-Schmidt walk, arXiv:1708.01079) is confirmed by multiple sources, e.g. arXiv:1806.04484 and arXiv:2207.03268 ('later work has since then closed the gap and given a polynomial time algorithm matching Banaszczyk's bound').
problems.statusDetails: At workshop time: $O(\log \min\{d, n\})$ [Bansal'10, Lovett-Meka'14, Rothvoss'15]. Since then Bansal-Dadush-Garg (FOCS 2016) and Bansal-Dadush-Garg-Lovett (2016/2017) achieve $O(\sqrt{\log \min\{d, n\}})$ constructively, matching Banaszczyk. The remaining challenge of a constant guarantee is equivalent to the Komlós conjecture.
